ARTICLE: 37.5a—Cases of those who make a confession: 1) knowing that someone will accuse them to court, 2) after they have fled (either to avoid punishment or various duties),22 or 3) after treason is already under way,23 22The various offenses involved are covered in Articles 457-464. 23See Article 251; Deloustal 411. The penalties are greatly increased for the plotters if their treason is actually under way.
will have their punishment reduced two degrees.
[4a] SUBCOMMENTARY:
Where the criminal
knows that someone will accuse him to the court or that an investigation will take place and confesses,
or where he has taken flight,
or where treason is already under way,
and when these kinds of offenses are discovered returns and confesses—
each such criminal will have the punishment for his offense reduced two degrees.
ARTICLE: 37.5b—If a person who has fled or whose treason is under way returns to his native place, even though he does not confess,
(returns to his native place)
it is considered the same.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Even though he does not confess
refers to not having confessed to the officials.
Returning to his native place
refers to returning to the place from which he first fled or committed treason.
These cases are still considered the same as under the law on confession
and punishment is reduced two degrees.
If his native place has changed,
return to such a changed place
is the same.
ARTICLE: 37.6—Cases involving those who injure or wound people,
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Injure
means to injure the body.
Wound
means to shed blood in making a wound.
Even though a personal retainer or slave is the one wounded or injured,
it is considered the same as the principle on commoners.
COMMENTARY:
If a person kills or wounds because of committing a crime and confesses,
he is exempted from punishment for the crime which was the cause of the killing or wounding.

But the law on intentionally killing or wounding is followed.24 24Article 281 punishes wounding someone during the course of a robbery by stran­gulation and killing by decapitation. Confession, however, would get those punish­ments reduced to life exile to 3,000 li.
If the killing or wounding was accidental,
the sentence follows the relevant law.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
If because of a robbery a criminal intentionally kills or wounds someone,
or if the owner of the goods is accidentally killed or wounded and the criminal confesses,
[4b] the criminal is exempted from punishment for robbery
and sentenced for intentionally killing or wounding.
If the killing or wounding was accidental,
the relevant law on accidents is followed.
Therefore, it is stated that if the killing or wounding was accidental, the sentence follows the relevant law.
ARTICLE: or articles which cannot be returned,
[20] SUBCOMMENTARY:
Reference to articles

means such things as pao and yin seals,25 tallies and ensigns (chieh 節),26 imperial decrees, official documents, armor, crossbows, flags, banners, forbidden military weapons, and proscribed books, 25See translation Chapter I, notes 138 and 141. 26See translation Chapter II, note 85.
which private households may not possess.27 27See the discussion on forbidden books in translation Chapter IV, note 47.
These types of things cannot be returned.
Confession where the original articles are present
refers to such things as cannot be returned.
But if the original articles are present,
the case is considered the same as under the law on exemption from punishment.
ARTICLE: or those who flee when the affair is discovered,
SUBCOMMENTARY:
If there is a robbery, the punishment is penal servitude.
If the criminal takes flight after the crime is discovered
and then returns after several days and confesses,
but the robbery has already been discovered,
even though he confesses, he will not be pardoned.
But the punishment for taking flight
will be reduced two degrees.

ARTICLE: or those who climb over boundary gates,28 or who have illicit sexual intercourse,2928Articles 82, 83, 87, and 88 cover the various forms of this offense. Simply climbing over a boundary gate without having the proper credentials was punished by one year of penal servitude. 29See Articles 410-415. Illicit sexual intercourse could be punished by as little as ninety blows with the heavy stick where the offense involved a commoner and a member of one of the inferior classes. On the other hand, a man who had illicit sexual intercourse with his father's concubine would be strangled.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
There are three kinds of offenses concerning boundary gates:
climbing over the boundary gate,
illegally passing through the boundary gate,
and falsifying a name and passing through the boundary gate.
Illegally passing through the boundary gate and passing over the boundary gate
are not pardoned by confession.
for falsifying a name and passing through the boundary gate.
But confession does get exemption from punishment
for illicit sexual intercourse by members of the inferior classes with commoners.
Confession does not get pardon
[5a] ARTICLE: or those who make unauthorized studies of the heavenly patterns

do not come within the principle on confession.3030The word patterns is used here because both astronomy and astrology are included. See the discussion in Needham, Science and Civilization in China, In, 193.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
The heavenly patterns are mystical and far away,
they may not be studied without authorization.
From injuring and wounding persons
down to the unauthorized study of the heavenly patterns,
none of these cases come within the principle on confession.
COMMENTARY: 37.1b—The original illicit goods are still repaid in accordance with the law.

involving collective prosecution or plotting treason or more by a relative who originally was within the one year degree of mourning, This means that only those who will not appear in court are prosecuted.
COMMENTARY: 37.3b—Should a person be arrested and accused to the court of crimes
both of these cases are considered the same as under the principle on confession.
This means that only those who will not appear in court are prosecuted.
COMMENTARY: 37.4b—If the confession of the amount of illicit goods is not complete,
the sentence may only be for the calculation of the value of the incomplete amount.
COMMENTARY: If a person kills or wounds because of committing a crime and confesses,
he is exempted from punishment for the crime which was the cause of the killing or wounding.
But the law on intentionally killing or wounding is followed.24
If the killing or wounding was accidental, the sentence follows the relevant law.
COMMENTARY: Where the original articles are present, confession
is the same as under the law on exemption from punishment.
COMMENTARY: Even though the crime is not confessed,
reduction of punishment for flight is allowed.
ARTICLE: 38.1a—All cases involving those who commit crimes and flee together
where those whose crime is less serious are able to arrest those whose crime is more serious and surrender (shou),
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Where a crime has been committed
and those who are in prison or who are not yet in prison flee together with those who have committed the same or a different offense,
and those whose punishment is life exile are able to arrest those who are sentenced to death,
or those who are sentenced to penal servitude are able to arrest those punished by life exile and surrender,
such are considered to be cases
where those whose crime is less serious are able to arrest those whose crime is more serious and surrender.
COMMENTARY:
Where the more serious offense requires the death penalty,
if the person is killed by the others who then surrender.
it is the same
SUBCOMMENTARY:
The article refers to the death penalty being required.
This does not mean that it must have already been sentenced
but that the death penalty is provided for by the crime
and that the criminal has fled.
If one whose offense is less serious kills him and comes to surrender,
it is considered the same as under the law on arrest and surrender.
Where those punished by life exile or less take flight,
and those with a lighter punishment are able to arrest those with a heavier punishment,

the law on arrest is comparable to that in the Articles on Arrest and Flight on those who flee.31 31Article 453. That is, if a criminal is killed while resisting arrest, his slayer will not be punished.
But if the prisoner has been sentenced to death,
arrest is not necessary.
Where it is more convenient to kill him,
this is considered the same as arrest.
[5b] ARTICLE: where the crimes are equally serious,
if some of the criminals are able to seize one-half or more of their fellows and surrender,
they will have their punishment canceled.
[21] SUBCOMMENTARY:
If five men, all of whom have committed crimes punishable by one hundred blows with the heavy stick,
flee together,
and one man has a repentant heart
and seizes another two men and surrenders,

this is considered to be seizing one-half or more [and surrendering].32 32Tai, General Principles, p. 358, adds here the character shou , "to surrender," even though no edition gives this reading. I have followed Tai's reading in order to have the passage make sense.
In this section on fleeing together and below,
both the original crime and the crime of flight are pardoned.
Therefore it is stated that their punishment will be canceled.
COMMENTARY:
38.1b—Cases not pardoned by ordinary amnesty
follow the ordinary law.3333See Articles 11 and 488. In addition to the ten abominations, several other particularly serious crimes were not pardoned by ordinary amnesty.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Cases not pardoned by ordinary amnesty
even though there be a great amnesty.
refer to such sentences as death or life exile,
disenrollment, resignation from occupied office, and removal from the community, which are still in effect
These types of offenses are not pardoned by amnesty.
Therefore, even if some of the criminals seize others and surrender,
they will not be exempted from punishment.
QUERY:
If ten men who are to be punished by one hundred blows with the heavy stick
flee together
and six return and surrender,
having seized two others who fled,
is this the same as seizing one-half or more, canceling punishment?
REPLY:
The article set forth in the law on mutual arrests
is based on a minority being able to arrest a majority,
or those whose offense is less serious being able to arrest those whose crime is more serious,
or where the offenses are of equal seriousness some of the criminals being able to seize one-half of their fellows.
Now six men together seizing two men
is rather a majority arresting a minority,
which according to the meaning of the article
does not provide for surrender getting pardon.
But where those who have fled from punishment surrender,
the original punishment for the offense will be reduced two degrees from that sentenced in accordance with the law.
If those whose offense is less serious are able to arrest those whose offense is more serious,
even though the latter are a minority,
[6a] pardon is given.
But where the offenses are of equal seriousness,
surrender does not gain pardon in case a majority of the criminals seize a minority,
but only if [at least] an equal number are seized.
FURTHER QUERY:
If two persons, A and B,
whose crimes are of equal seriousness
flee together
and A seizes B and surrenders,
does A get exemption from punishment or not?
REPLY:
The article mentions that if some of the criminals seize one-half or more of their fellows and surrender,
their punishment will be canceled.
If A and B flee together
and A seizes B,
the crime of flight has been ended,
there are no others in flight.
If seizure of one-half of the criminals gets exemption from punishment,34 34Kushould be read tsui, following the KHCPTS edition.
for seizure of all others who took flight?
how much more then should A be pardoned
If ten persons under sentence of death
flee together
and five arrest five,
this is a case of one-half surrendering having seized the other one-half.
Since the law has opened the way for arrest and surrender,35 35Shou pushould be read pu shou, which is the order in every other occurrence of this phrase in the Code.
such cases will get complete exemption from punishment.
FURTHER QUERY:
If relatives of the fifth or closer degree of mourning commit a crime and flee together,
is the same law on arrest and sur­render applicable or not?
REPLY:
(by relatives of the fifth or closer degree of mourning)
Accusations to the court in cases of crimes committed by relatives of the fifth or closer degree of mourning are not provided for.
They may conceal those who flee and still be permitted reduction of punishment.
How then can they arrest and send each other to the court?
This principle was set forth for persons of non-kin status
and is not a text concerned with relatives.
Cases of arrest and surrender involving relatives
gain reduction of the sentence for taking flight,
but the punishment for the original offense is not pardoned.
Thus it still follows the law on wounding, killing, or accusing relatives to the court.
But where the crime is plotting treason or more,
the article on arrest and surrender is followed.3636See Article 46. For such crimes as plotting treason, it is not permissable for relatives to conceal each others' crimes.
[22] ARTICLE: 38.2a—Cases of crimes that are the result of a criminal,
and where the criminal dies a natural death,
reduce the punishment for the original crime two degrees.
[6b] SUBCOMMENTARY:
Crimes that are the result of a criminal
refer to such crimes as concealing criminals,

or giving them aid,37 or failing as a guarantor, or giving false evidence.38 37Article 468 punishes this crime if done knowingly with a sentence only one degree less than that of the criminal who was concealed. 38Someone who guaranteed that a criminal would not run away would be punished only two degrees less than the sentence given that criminal if flight occurred. If someone gave false evidence, he also would be punished only two degrees less than the sentence given his victim. See Articles 386 and 387.
Should the criminal die a natural death rather than being executed,
the punishment of those involved because of him is reduced two degrees.
ARTICLE: 38.2b—Cases where the criminal confesses or meets with imperial grace and is pardoned or has his punishment reduced
also follow this law on the criminal being pardoned or having his punishment reduced.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
This refers to crimes that are the result of a criminal,
where later the criminal confesses or meets with imperial grace and is pardoned or has his punishment reduced.
Some criminals get a complete pardon,
others have their punishments reduced one or two degrees and the like.
But all cases follow this law on the criminal gaining complete pardon, reduction of punishment, or a decrease of sentence.
ARTICLE: 38.2c—Cases that require substitution of blows with the heavy stick or redemption by payment of copper,
each follow the principles on the heavy stick or redemption by payment of copper.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
As for substituting blows with the heavy stick,
should an official bondsman or a slave commit a crime punished by life exile and be given aid by someone,
when the official bondsman or slave is caught,
the punishment of life exile is replaced by two hundred blows with the heavy stick.39 39See Article 28.
The person who gave aid has his punishment reduced from that of two hundred blows with the heavy stick
and not from the punishment of life exile.
Should the criminal himself be allowed redemption by payment of copper,
the punishment for those who gave aid also follows the law on redemption by payment of copper.
They need not use office to replace punishment or have blows with the heavy stick substituted, or be sent to labor.
QUERY:
If an official bondsman, and so forth, commits a crime punished by life exile,
two hundred blows with the heavy stick are substituted.
But how many degrees of reduction are required for those who give aid?
REPLY:
In cases where blows with the heavy stick are substituted for crimes punished by penal servitude,
each degree of penal servitude adds twenty blows,
with a maximum of two hundred blows
replacing three years of penal servitude.40 40Article 27.
If the [7a] punishment extends to life exile,
this is also two hundred blows with the heavy stick.
Where reduction of punishment is required in cases where blows with the heavy stick are substituted for life exile,
the text gives no degree of reduction.
By analogy
it follows the one degree of reduction for penal servitude—
one hundred eighty blows with the heavy stick.
COMMENTARY: Where the more serious offense requires the death penalty,
if the person is killed by the others who then surrender.
it is the same
COMMENTARY: 38.1b—Cases not pardoned by ordinary amnesty
follow the ordinary law.33
ARTICLE: 39.1—In all cases of goods and articles taken by robbery or fraud, confession to the owner of the goods
is considered to be the same as confession to the officials.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Robbery
refers to robbery by force or by stealth.
Fraud
refers to taking someone's goods and articles by fraud or cheating.41 41Article 373 sentences this crime as comparable to robbery.
But if the criminal repents his fault
and confesses to the owner of the goods,
it is considered the same as confession to the officials.
In cases where the criminal confesses to the owner of the goods upon knowing that someone is going to accuse him to the court,
he will still get a reduction of two degrees of punishment.
QUERY:
If A robs B of goods worth five p'i of silk,
and confesses to B,
who then takes goods worth ten p'i of silk from A
as the original and doubled illicit goods,
what is the proper punishment?
[23] REPLY:
According to the article,
those who confess only repay the original illicit goods.42 42See Article 37.
If A confesses to B,
who, therefore, takes in excess of his original articles,
and if B is an official other than a supervisory or custodial official,
then he has taken goods because of an affair,

and is sentenced to punishment for illicit goods gained through malfeasance .4343Article 389. Depending upon the amount of goods, the punishment could range from twenty blows with the light stick to a maximum of three years of penal servitude.
ARTICLE: 39.2a—In cases of other illicit goods where prosecution is required,
if the criminal repents his fault and returns them to the owner,
his sentence will be reduced three degrees below the original punishment.
[7b] SUBCOMMENTARY:
Other illicit goods
refers to those other than from robbery or fraud,
but where punishment is required.
even though he does not make a confession to the officials,
If the criminal is able to repent his fault and return the goods to their owner,
his sentence will be reduced three degrees below the original punishment.
If an official has subverted the law and taken bribes worth ten p'i of silk,
this is punished by life exile.
If he then repents his faults and returns them to the owner,
he gets a reduction of three degrees of punishment
and is sentenced to two years of penal servitude.
Thus it is stated that sentencing
follows the principle below.4444See Article 53. Crimes sentenced as comparable cannot force an official's resigna­tion from office or disenrollment.
ARTICLE: 39.2b—Cases which require that the owner of the goods be prosecuted
also have their punishment reduced in accordance with this principle.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Required prosecution for the owner of the goods

refers to cases of officials taking bribes and subverting the law or not subverting the law, or taking goods and articles in the area under their supervision, or of gaining illicit goods through malfeasance.
In each of these cases the giver of goods is also punished.45 45However, his punishment is reduced five degrees below that of the official who took the bribe. See Article 140.
If one takes illicit goods from a person and repents his faults and returns them to the owner,
he gets a reduction of three degrees of punishment.
The owner of the goods' sentence is also reduced three degrees below the original punishment.
QUERY:
If someone sells or exchanges government property
and later wants to return it
but the original articles have already been expended
and new articles are substituted,
does this kind of repentance of fault
get exemption from punishment or not?
REPLY:
If a person wants to return the original articles,
he gets exemption from calculating the value of the illicit goods in determining punishment
and is sentenced for robbery where nothing has been taken.46 46Article 282 punishes this offense with fifty blows with the light stick.
If one no longer has the original government property
and uses new goods to replace it,
even though there is double payment by one's own goods,
the crime of trading government property still remains.

[8a] 47 ARTICLE: 40.1a—All cases of public offenses by those who work together make 47Articles 40 and 41 have been translated and discussed by Bünger, "Verantwortlich­keit der Beamten." See also Article 14.
the positions of senior officer,
second officer,
executive officer,
and chief clerk each one class.
Each person is the principal for that which originated with him.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Working together
refers to officials who sign documents together.
Public offenses
refers to there being no secret crookedness.
If the Supreme Court of Justice makes a mistake in sentencing a crime,
then its president48 is the senior officer, 48Both here and below, t'ai-ching 太卿 should be read ta-ching 大卿, following the SPTK edition.
the vice president and the revisory judges are the second officers,
the assistants are the executive officers,
and archivists and the secretaries49 are the chief clerks. 49Lishould be read shih, following the KHCPTS edition.
These are the four classes.
Each person is the principal for that which originates with him
means that if a chief clerk makes a mistake in examination of the petition,
then he is the principal.
The assistants are the second-degree accessories,
the vice president and the two revisory judges are the third-degree accessories,
and the president is the fourth-degree accessory.
The registrars and scribes are also fourth-degree accessories.
If the mistake in sentence originated with an assistant,
then he is the principal,
the vice president and the two revisory judges are second-degree accessories,
the president is the third-degree accessory,
and the chief50 clerks are the fourth-degree accessories. 50Chu 主 should precede tien 典, following the KHCPTS edition.
The registrar and scribe are also considered to be fourth-degree accessories.
[24] COMMENTARY:
In cases where the mistake is due to different sentences by executive officers or higher officials,
only such officials are prosecuted.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
If one revisory judge makes a mistake because of differing with the sentence given by the assistant,
and another revisory judge agrees with him,
then both revisory [8b] judges are principals in the crime.
If one revisory judge first allows the assistant's sentence,
and only then does another revisory judge disagree,
the one who disagrees is sentenced as the principal,
the one who agreed with the assistant is not punished.
If the sentence given by an assistant is correct,
one revisory judge's sentence is mistakenly in disagreement with that sentence,
and the later revisory judge only states that he follows the sentence,
then his offense is the same as that of the earlier revisory judge.
But if he states that he follows the sentence given by the assistant,
then the later revisory judge is not at fault.
Should the president and vice president disagree,
such mistakes also follow this principle.
by second officers or higher officials,
Where there is mistaken reasoning because of disagreements
and where collective responsibility is required,
only the senior officer and such officials as examine or recheck the documents are punished.
Those officials below them are not prosecuted.
If there is a mistake by a second officer or a lower official,
or one is right and the other wrong,
but the decision of the senior officer follows the correct formal law,
then the other officials are all exempted from punishment.
All offices, both in the capital and the provinces, follow this principle.
QUERY:
If an executive officer's sentence is contrary or mistaken,
and that of the second officer disagrees with him and is correct
but the senior officer does not follow the sentence of the second officer,
rather agreeing with that given by the executive officer,
then what punishment does each of them get?
REPLY:
If a case is sent up for review
and only the second officer is correct,
then those above and below him are both exempted from punishment.
If the sentence was proper but its administration was contrary or mistaken,
then those who did so are punished according to the law.
But if the second officer and the senior officer were correct,
the other officials are not prosecuted.
ARTICLE: 40.1b—Where offices have not been filled,
the law on these four classes of officials is still followed.
Where there are not four classes of officials,
[9a] those classes that exist are punished.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Within the four classes of officials
if there are posts that have not been filled,
although only one officer makes the decision, should his sentence be contrary or mistaken,
four classes of officials are still prosecuted.
If the post of president of the Supreme Court of Justice,
or of an assistant, or of a revisory judge has been filled,
and his decision is contrary or mistaken,
he is the principal.
The official who rechecks his decision is still to be considered the fourth-degree accessory.
Where there are not four classes of officials
refers51 to such places as customs stations and military outposts 51Wei 爲 should be read wei 謂, following the KHCPTS edition.
where there are no second officers.
From the assistants to the commander at the customs barrier,
including the chief clerks,
there are only three classes.
If the chief clerk goes contrary to the law or is mistaken in examining a petition,
the assistant is the second-degree accessory
and the commander is the third-degree accessory.
The scribe is also considered to be a third-degree accessory.
In lower-grade prefectures and counties, the market supervisors have only two clerks.
Thus only the two classes of offices filled are included in punishment.
ARTICLE: 40.2—If among those who work together there is a private offense,52 52See the definition of private offense in Article 17.
and the officials who are collectively responsible do not know the circumstances,
they are sentenced for having made a mistake.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Working together
refers to officials and clerks who are jointly involved in a decision.
If there is a mistaken
or deliberate violation of correct principle,
those other officials who are jointly involved in the decision but who did not know of or take part in the circumstances of the private offense,
are sentenced for having made a mistake.
If someone commits an offense punished by one year of penal servitude,
and the executive [25] officer twists principle in sentencing so that the criminal is exempted from punishment,
the other officials who are not aware of the circumstances
are punished according to the law on mistakenly decreasing punishment.53 53See Article 487.
The official who has committed the private offense is the principal;
those who were not aware of the circumstances are the accessories.
Thus there are four classes of officials sentenced.
A mistaken decrease of sentence has the punishment reduced five degrees,
a mistaken increase in sentence has the punishment reduced three degrees, and the like.
The other officials, as compared with the one who decided the crime,
are sentenced for having made a mistake and get a reduction of three [9b] degrees of punishment.54 54That is, three degrees below the proper punishment.
And, as stated, they are sentenced for having made a mistake.
Each offense follows the specific article.
QUERY:
Should a chief clerk add to or delete from the text of a case
and by fraud or cheat obtain illicit goods worth five p'i of silk,
and the executive officer, not being aware of these circumstances,
sentence the case according to the added or deleted circumstances,
it is not yet known if the executive officer gets a reduction of punishment for a mistake concerning the illicit goods obtained by fraud or cheat,
or a reduction of punishment for a mistake concerning addition to or deletion from the text of an official document.
REPLY:
In accordance with this article,
offenses are all prosecuted according to the sentence.
The crime of obtaining illicit goods lies outside the case.
The text of the case which was added to or deleted from has been circulated,
and the sentence may only follow such additions or deletions,
and not the illicit goods.
FURTHER QUERY:
If the executive officer and the chief clerk commit a private offense
by deliberately lessening a punishment of life exile,
and the second officer and senior officer do not know the circumstances,
how is the punishment for principal and accessories to be sentenced?
REPLY:
Where the chief clerk is the principal,
he is sentenced to life exile.
The executive officer is the second-degree accessory,
and he is sentenced to three years of penal servitude.
For those who do not know the circumstances,
the law on committing a public offense by mistake is followed.
Including those punished for a public offense there would be four classes.
The second officer would be the third-degree accessory
and his punishment would be reduced two degrees below that of the clerk.
There would be a further reduction of five degrees of punishment for a mistaken decrease of sentence,
so that the reduction of punishment of seven degrees from life exile
would be ninety blows with the heavy stick.
The senior officer would get still another degree of reduction of punishment,
or eighty blows with the heavy stick.
Where the prisoner has been released and seized again
or a relevant principle requires reduction of punishment,55 55See Article 10.
the relevant law is followed in each case.
ARTICLE: 40.3a—Thus if other officials or higher officials examine the case and are not aware of the circumstances,
each gets a further degree of reduction of punishment.
40.3b—If lower officials are not aware of the circumstances,
[10a] they also get a further degree of reduction of punishment.
Each is still the principal for that which originated with him.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Other officials
refers to those of nearby prefectures, counties, or departments
as well as those of various superior prefectures, courts, and directorates, which are independent of each other.
Higher officials
are those of the various offices in the capital vis-à-vis the departments and tribunals, those of the various prefectures vis-à-vis the Department of State,
those of the various counties vis-à-vis the prefectures, and the like.
If a prefecture sends up a document to the Department of State
that has an error or mistake,
and the official of the department is not aware of it,
the punishment for the department official's responsibility as principal
is reduced one degree below the prefecture's responsibility as principal.
Those who work together are the four classes given in the law and their punishment as principal and accessories is progressively reduced.
Should other officials not be aware of the error,
this principle is also followed.
If a departmental official sends down a document to a prefecture, which has an error or mistake
that the prefectural official is not aware of,
the punishment for the prefectural official's responsibility as principal is reduced two degrees below the departmental official's responsibility as principal.
Those who work together are the four classes and their punishments as principal and accessories are progressively reduced following this law.
ARTICLE: 40.4—Officials who examine or recheck documents
are punished the same as the lowest accessories.
[26] SUBCOMMENTARY:
Examine
refers to scribes in the various offices who investigate errors at the time when documents are issued.
Recheck
refers to administrators who sign their names as final approval.
All such persons are punished the same as the lowest accessories.
If there are four classes of officials
they are punished the same as the fourth class of accessories,
and it is the same if there be three
or two classes of officials involved.
If there are no officials to examine and recheck,
then the executive officer approves and rechecks at the time when the document is issued.
If there are contradictions or mistakes,
the punishment is for the sentence.
The rechecking and examination of the document is not prosecuted.
[10b] ARTICLE: 40.5—In matters that must be memorialized, if officials make mistakes
in checking and proofreading, or if in the departmental examination of documents the officials do not correct the mistakes,
such officials have their punishment reduced one degree below that of the lowest accessories.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Matters that must be memorialized by the Department of State
pass through the Imperial Chancellery
and the documents are dispatched there.
In accordance with the ordinance and following the statute,
"[The document is] first checked by the scribe of the Imperial Chancellery,
proofread by the grand secretary of the Imperial Chancellery,
examined by the vice president of the Imperial Chancellery,
and re-examined by the president of the Imperial Chancellery.''56 56Niida, Statutes, p. 546.
If there are contradictions or mistakes,
in accordance with the law these must be corrected,
and the document is sent back to the office of the Department of State.
If these inconsistencies are real
and not corrected,
the scribe and those above him
have their punishments reduced one degree below those of the lowest accessories in the Department of State.
There is no text on progressive reduction of punishment.
Thus the president and those below him
have their punishment reduced equally one degree.
This article considers reduction of punishment to below that for the lowest accessories
to be the lightest.
If there should be progressively further reduction of punishment,
others would not be prosecuted at all.
The law on correction of mistakes
is only for scribes and those above them.
for chief clerks who handled the document.
Therefore, the article provides no punishment
ARTICLE: 40.6-If the phraseology of a document is obscure
so that there is no way to know it through examination,
this is not punished.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
The phraseology of a document is obscure
means that words have been left out, or there are mistakes,
or there have been additions or deletions of crimes and circumstances.
If the phraseology is obscure and unclear,
those who review the case will find it difficult to be aware of such mistakes.
Therefore, it is stated57 that other officials and those below them 57Ku yün 故云 should be inserted here, following the SPTK edition.
who review the case without being aware of the mistakes
will all be exempted from punishment.
Therefore it is stated that there is no prosecution.
[24] COMMENTARY: In cases where the mistake is due to different sentences by executive officers or higher officials,
only such officials are prosecuted.
[11a] ARTICLE: 41.1a—In all cases where there are mistakes in public affairs
and one of those involved becomes aware of the mistake himself and brings it out,
the offense will be pardoned.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Mistakes in public matters
refer to cases of offenses due to public affairs that have no private crookedness.
If one of those involved becomes aware of the mistake himself and brings it out before the matter has been discovered,
he will be exempted from punishment for the mistake.
The meaning of "to become aware of and bring out''
is different from that of confession.
If a person confesses58 58Tzu 自 should precede shou 首, following the KHCPTS edition.
knowing that someone will accuse him to the court,
there is a reduction of two degrees of punishment.
But this article on becoming aware of and bringing out has no such text.
If an official speaks of the mistake himself before it is discovered,
he will be exempted from punishment.
ARTICLE: 41.1b—Where collective responsibility is required,
if one person becomes aware of and brings out the mistake,
the others are also pardoned.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Where collective responsibility is required
refers to senior officers and below
and chief clerks and above as well as officials who examine and recheck—all those who together decide and sign the documents on a case.
If one of them becomes aware of and brings out the mistake,
the others are also pardoned.
Should the officials who examine and recheck bring out [27] the mistake in examination and the affair is connected with private crookedness,
the officials are punished according to the law.
But if it is a public offense
and the circumstances have no private crookedness,
even if the mistake is brought out by officials who examine and recheck,
none of them is responsible for the offense.
ARTICLE: 41.2—Should the sentence be mistaken
and the punishment already have been administered,
this article is not applicable.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Should the sentence be mistaken and the punishment already have been administered
refers to the death sentence or blows with the light or heavy stick having already been administered,
or those sentenced to life exile already being at the place of exile and having finished their labor,
or those sentenced to penal servitude having finished their labor.
If these types of punishment have already been administered,
then even though the officials themselves become aware of and bring out the mistake,
the offense does not come within this principle on exemption [11b] from punishment.
Rather each official is sentenced according to the law on mistaken increase of punishment.
Therefore it is stated that this law is not applicable.
For such cases as a person being wrongly sentenced to two years of penal servitude,
and when he has done one year of labor,
only then does an official become aware of and bring out the mistake,
the official is accordingly exempted from punishment for the one year that was not done
and which he became aware of and brought out.
The one year that has already been served
is punished following the law on mistaken increase of punishment and the punishment is reduced three degrees
to eighty blows with the heavy stick.
ARTICLE: 41.3—Where there is a delay in official documents
and collective responsibility is required,
if one person becomes aware of59 and brings out the delay, 59Both here and below chueh 覺 should precede chu 擧, following the SPTK edition.
the others will also be pardoned.
But the chief clerk will not be exempted from punishment.
If the chief clerk himself becomes aware of and brings out the delay,
his punishment will also be reduced two degrees.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Documents
refer to official cases.
"Matters of least importance have a five-day time limit,
matters of medium importance have a ten-day time limit,
and matters of greatest importance have a twenty-day time limit. ''60 60Niida, Statutes, p. 595.

Thirty days is the limit for those involving penal servitude or more after the sentence has been accepted by the criminal.61 61The meaning of pien 辨 or fu-pien 服辨 is for the criminal to accept his sentence. See Yang, "Notes on Maspero's Les Documents Chinois," p. 154.
If these limits are exceeded without the case being finished,
it is called delay.
Should an official become aware of the delay himself and bring it out,
he and the others involved will get a complete pardon.
Only the chief clerk will not be exempted from punishment.
If the chief clerk becomes aware of the delay himself and brings it out,
he will also have his punishment reduced two degrees.
Because the officials did not bring it out,
the chief officer and those below will all have their punishment reduced [only] two degrees.
If an official and the chief clerk jointly sign and bring out the delay,
the official will get exemption from punishment
and the chief clerk's sentence will be reduced two degrees.
When imperial decrees or edicts
are completed and are to be issued,
there is a time limit for their being copied.
For two hundred pages or less, the time limit is two days.
For more than two hundred pages,
one day is added for each two hundred pages
with a maximum of five days for any number.
The Commentary states:
(an amnesty)
"Even though the number of pages of an amnesty is more,

the time limit for copying may not [12a] exceed three days. ''6262This commentary does not appear in the Code. But from the sentence above, the phrase which begins "For two hundred pages..." to the end of this quotation from the commentary is found in the Statutes, p. 598.
The time limit for this type of copying
is stated to be after the document has been completed.
According to the statute,
for issuing completed imperial decrees and edicts,
there is no separate time limit
that is, it must be done on the same day that they are completed.
If the statute on time limits is violated,
this is delay.
If there is delay and the one who caused it becomes aware of it and brings it out himself,
it is considered the same as the law on official documents.
Thus it is a public offense
with four classes of officials sentenced,
each as principal for that which originated with him.
If there is any connection with private crookedness and the delay is deliberate,
then it is considered the same as the law on private offenses.
QUERY:
Public offenses are collective,
and the punishment is according to the divisions and grades of officials involved.
If one of them becomes aware of and brings out the delay,
the others also are pardoned.
Delay of a case then is a public offense
and the officials who recheck the documents are also collectively responsible.
But if the officials who examine and recheck bring out the delay,
for what reason are the other officials punished?
REPLY:
As for mistakes that are public offenses,
such affairs can be found and corrected.
So if one person becomes aware of the mistake and brings it out,
the others will also be pardoned.
But as for matters that need to be administered, if they are delayed or held up
this is not the same principle as for mistakes.
Since the delay has been brought out by the officials who recheck such documents,
the responsible officials are not exempted from sentence.
ARTICLE: 42.1—In all cases where crimes are committed collectively
the person who formulates the plan (tsao-yi 造意) is the principal.
The accessories have their sentences reduced one degree.
42.2a—If the members of a household commit a crime collectively,
only the person highest in generation, or oldest of the same generation is prosecuted.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Cases where crimes are committed collectively
refer to crimes committed collectively by two or more persons.
The person who first formulated the plan is the principal,
the others are all [12b] accessories.
Cases where the members of a household commit a crime collectively

refers to crimes committed collectively by a man together with his paternal grandfather, his father, his sons and grandsons in the male line, his paternal uncles, his younger brothers, and his nephews in the male line.
Only the person highest in generation, or oldest of the same generation of those who dwell together is prosecuted.
Those younger in generation or age are not punished.
COMMENTARY:
In cases involving those who by law cannot be prosecuted,
the punishment devolves on the next oldest in generation or age.
Highest in generation, or oldest of the same generation
refers to males.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Those who by law cannot be prosecuted
refers to those who are eighty years of age or more,
ten years of age or less, or are incapacitated.63 63See Article 30.
In such cases the punishment devolves on the next oldest in generation or age.
Highest in generation, or oldest of the same generation refers to males.
If a woman who is the highest in generation or the oldest of the same generation
commits a crime together with males who are younger,
even though the woman formulated the plan,
only the males are prosecuted.
ARTICLE: 42.2b—In cases where the members of a household encroach upon or injure people,
they are sentenced as principal and accessories following the laws on encroaching upon or wounding persons of commoner status.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Encroach upon means robbery of goods and articles by stealth.
Injure refers to such crimes as assault, beating, killing, and wounding.
If a father and sons together with other members of the household commit such crimes together,
the law regarding persons of non-kin status is followed.
and persons are encroached upon or injured,
In such cases prosecution is not limited to the eldest person in generation or age.
ARTICLE: If supervisory or custodial officials collectively commit crimes together with commoners,
even though a commoner formulates the plan,
the supervisory or custodial official is the principal.
The commoners are prosecuted as ordinary accessories.
[13a] SUBCOMMENTARY:
Supervisory and custodial officials
are explained later.64 64See Article 54.
Even suppose an outsider [that is, a non-official] puts forward the plan,
if he together with a chief clerk of the Bureau of the Treasury of the Left robs the granary of goods worth five p'i of silk,
even though the outsider formulated the plan.65 65See Article 283.
the chief clerk is the principal
and is sentenced to two years of penal servitude,
The outsider is sentenced as an ordinary accessory to robbery,

which is punished by one hundred blows with the heavy stick.66.66Article 282 punishes this offense by one year of penal servitude, which reduced one degree would be one hundred blows with the heavy stick.
COMMENTARY: In cases involving those who by law cannot be prosecuted,
the punishment devolves on the next oldest in generation or age.
Highest in generation, or oldest of the same generation
refers to males.
ARTICLE: 43.1—All cases where crimes are committed collectively yet the basic punishments are different,
even though the principal and accessories have committed the same crime,
punish the crime according to the specific articles on principal and accessories.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
If relatives within the five degrees of mourning
collectively with others beat or accuse their relatives to the court, or encroach upon or rob their goods and articles,
even though the crime was collective
yet the specific punishments are different.
If A brings in an outsider, B, and they together beat A's [29] older brother,
A is the principal
and is punished by two and one-half years of penal servitude.67 67See Article 328.
B is the accessory to ordinary assault.
Since he was not the initiator and did not actually strike the blow (hsia-shou 下手),
he gets a further degree of reduction of punishment
to twenty blows with the light stick.6868See Article 308. Thus he gets two degrees of reduction of punishment below the forty blows with the light stick for assault.

Further, if a person of a lower generation, or of the same generation but younger than other household members brings in another person and they together rob his own household of goods and articles worth ten p'i of silk,
the person of a lower generation, or of the same generation but younger than other household members is the principal
and is punished by thirty blows with the light stick.69 69Article 288.
The other person is the accessory

and is punished by one year of penal servitude.70 70Article 288 makes Article 282 applicable for the accessory, whose punishment is reduced one degree below the one and one-half years of penal servitude for the crime.
However, this punishment is reduced one degree below that for ordinary robbery
to one hundred blows with the heavy stick....
This principle encompasses many offenses,
which cannot all be recorded.
But cases where the principal and accessories have committed the same crime,
yet the basic punishments are different,
[13b] all follow this law.
ARTICLE: 43.2—If a specific article refers to "all,''
then the crime does not distinguish between principal and accessories.
If it does not refer to "all,''
then this law on principal and accessories is followed.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
It is submitted that in the Articles on Violence and Robbery:
"Those who plot to kill a relative of a higher generation, or of the same generation but older than themselves within the second degree of mourning, or maternal grandparents
will all be decapitated. ''71 71Article 253; Deloustal 415.
In such cases as this,
where the specific article refers to "all,''
the crime does not distinguish between principal and accessories.
If the specific article does not refer to "all,''
the sentence follows the law on principal and accessories.
Thus the Articles on Violence and Robbery also state:
"Those who plot to kill people
are punished with three years of penal servitude.''
If two persons together plot to kill a person
but the crime has not yet been carried out,
the one who formulated the plan is the principal
and is punished by three years of penal servitude.
The accessory
is punished by two and one-half years of penal servitude.
In such cases as this,
which do not speak of "all,''
the law on principal and accessories is followed.
ARTICLE: 43.3—In cases of robbery by force, as well as illicit sexual intercourse,
kidnapping persons to be slaves,
entering without authorization (lan-ju 闌入),
taking flight, illegally passing through or climbing over customs barriers, palisades, walls, or hedges,
no distinction is made between principal and accessories also.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Those who rob by force
use strength and power.72 72This is the definition of robbery by force given in Article 281.
Illicit sexual intercourse
is committed by the persons themselves,73 73See note 29 of this chapter.
so that there are no principals and accessories.

In kidnapping persons to be slaves,74 74Kidnapping persons and selling them as slaves was punished by strangulation. If they were sold as personal retainers, the penalty was life exile to 3,000 li, and if as a wife, concubine, son, or grandson, the penalty was two years of penal servitude. See Article 292.
the principle is the same as robbery by force.
Entering without authorization

refers to entering the palace or other forbidden place without authorization.75 75This offense is punished by two years of penal servitude or more, depending upon the circumstances and how far into the palace the criminal went. See Articles 58-60; Deloustal 50-52.
Each of these crimes is committed by the criminal himself
so there is also no distinction between principals and accessories.
(taking flight)
An example of taking flight is ten men who are all doing military service
and all of them neglect their duties.76 76See Article 457. The minimum punishment was one year of penal servitude for one day of absence from duty.
Illegally pass through
without having a passport.77 77See note 28 of this chapter.
refers to illegally going through a customs barrier gate
Climb over
refers to not going through the gate.
Customs barrier refers to a place where travelers are investigated.
[14a] Palisade refers to a place with ditches and stake fences.
Walls refer to the walls of palace and government buildings.
Hedges refer to walls that are not made of pounded earth, but which are secured by hedges and the like.
From robbery by force on down,
all of these offenses are sentenced as formal crimes.
Therefore, it is stated that there is no distinction between principals and accessories.
ARTICLE: 44.1—All cases in which crimes are committed collectively and the criminals take flight,
when the one who is caught states that the other who is still at large is the principal
and there are no other witnesses
provide for him to be sentenced to the punishment as an accessory.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
If two persons, A and B,
obtain articles by fraud or cheating,
this is punished by one year of penal servitude.78 78See Article 373. This crime is sentenced as robbery, so the amount of the fraud here is goods worth five p'i of silk.
A really was the principal
and is seized.
B originally was the accessory
but has taken flight.
A, upon being investigated and questioned (chu-wen 鞫問),
states that B was the principal,
and there are no witnesses.
A then is sentenced as the accessory
to one hundred blows with the heavy stick.79 79Article 42 reduces the punishment of accessories by one degree below that of the principal in an offense.
This is called sentencing him to punishment as an accessory.
ARTICLE: Later B, who had taken flight, is seized
and states that the first person, A, was the principal
and upon investigation and questioning this proves to be true.
A is then sentenced as the principal.
However, the previous punishment
is included in the later total.
[30] SUBCOMMENTARY:
If the criminal who was seized later, B,
states that A was the principal,
and upon investigation and questioning A
states that this is true,
he is then sentenced as the principal
to one year of penal servitude.
[14b] A is a commoner
and the one hundred blows with the heavy stick that have already been administered
must have their redemption value
deducted from the one year of penal servitude,
which can be redeemed by twenty chin of copper.
The redemption value of one hundred blows with the heavy stick is ten chin of copper,
which cancels one-half year of penal servitude,
A is sent to labor for one-half year of penal servitude.8080Article 3 gives the equivalents of penal servitude and amounts of copper.
so that in accordance with the law,
If A had been the only adult member of his household,
so that one hundred blows with the heavy stick had already been administered,
and he were now sentenced to one year of penal servitude,
which is equivalent to one hundred and twenty blows with the heavy stick,
then twenty more blows are administered.81 81See Article 27.
Thus the previous punishment
is included in the later total.
QUERY:
Two persons, A and B, commit a crime of robbery
equivalent to that punished by life exile.
A originally formulated the plan
and B was an accessory.
But when the affair is discovered, B takes flight.
Thereupon A states that B was the principal
and the officials sentence A as the accessory.
He is sentenced to three years of penal servitude
and when his labor is finished,
B is seized.
A admits that he is the principal,
further A is a commoner,
what is the sentence?
REPLY:
The punishment of life exile is equivalent to four years of penal servitude.
Further, it is stated:
"An increase of penal servitude to life exile
is equal to one additional year of penal servitude. ''82 82This quotation from Article 487 is not exact.
Cumulative sentences of penal servitude and life exile that require labor
may not exceed four years.
Even though this person has fraudulently falsified the circumstances to the officials,
he may not be sentenced again to life exile,
but only to one year of penal servitude.
If the sentence were life exile with added labor,
which itself carries three years of penal servitude,
even though the criminal had already been sent to labor and had labored for three years,
he still would be sent into life exile at a greater distance.
But since the previous punishment would be included,
this would cancel forced labor in a fixed place at the place of exile.
ARTICLE: 44.1b—If one has already turned over articles as redemption
and their return is later required,
they are returned.
[15a] SUBCOMMENTARY:
If a ninth-rank official, A,
commits a crime punished by one year of penal servitude
and fraudulently gets reduced punishment as an accessory,
he redeems the sentence of one hundred blows with the heavy stick
with ten chin of copper.
Now, if he is later sentenced as principal
to one year of penal servitude,
this cancels a single office of the ninth rank in replacing the sentence of penal servitude.
The ten chin of copper which has been paid previously is returned to him....
ARTICLE: 44.2—Where punishments have been increased or decreased,whether
they are light or heavy,
this article is still followed.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Suppose a case is of the type in which the supervisory official
increases someone's punishment.
A person has committed a crime punished by one year of penal servitude
and has only one office of the ninth rank.
The official increases his punishment
and sentences him to two years of penal servitude.
His office replaces one year
and the remaining penal servitude is redeemed by payment of copper.
Later at a further hearing and questioning
it is determined that the punishment should have been only one year of penal servitude.
The articles for redemption of the previous increase of one year of punishment are returned.
As for reduction of punishment,
if a person holds two administrative positions
both of which are of the ninth rank or above
and commits a crime punished by two years of penal servitude
and the official reduces this to one and one-half years,
one office replaces one year of penal servitude.
The remaining one-half year
does not cancel the other office
so it is redeemed by ten chin of copper.
Upon investigation it becomes known that the first sentence was a mistake,
so that two offices must be used to replace two years of penal servitude.
The articles for redemption that had previously been turned over are returned to the owner.
Further, a commoner commits a crime punished by three years of penal servitude.
The official sentences him to one year of penal servitude
and after the labor is completed, the matter is discovered.
He must again be sentenced to another two years of penal servitude.
Since the first [31] year's has been completed,
the criminal must later be sent to an additional two years of labor.
[15h] ARTICLE: 44.3—In cases where there is subversion of the law in increasing persons' sentences of penal servitude,
the penal servitude is calculated in terms of the labor service
exemption tax and cancels taxes and labor services, as does the value of copper for redemption of punishment.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Reference to subversion of the law in increasing persons' sentences of penal servitude
is not limited to the innocent,
but includes all cases where penal servitude and labor were not required but were nevertheless sentenced.
This is what is meant by subversion of the law in increasing penal servitude.
Subversion of the law in increase of sentence for a whole year
is made clear in the texts of the commentaries.
Where labor is not a full fifty days
and the labor imposed by subversion of the law
is calculated as twenty days or less,
each day cancels one day from the adult service exemption tax.
Thirty-five days
also cancel the tiao taxes.
Other days fewer than fifty
do not further cancel taxes or services.
As does the value of copper for redemption of punishment
refers to where the son of an official of the seventh rank or above
is sentenced to one year of penal servitude through subversion of the law.
The bodily labor of the labor service exemption tax
is canceled by the redemption value of one year of penal servitude.
The labor service exemption tax is calculated and set off against the copper.
If not completely used up,
the excess copper is returned.
If the copper is used up without the labor service exemption tax being completely canceled,
the remainder
is not paid.
Taxes and labor services
are canceled according to the law above.
The offense of the supervisory official
follows the law on deliberate or mistaken increase of sentence.
If an adolescent male sixteen years of age or above who has the right of redemption by payment of copper
commits a crime punished by one hundred blows with the heavy stick,
and the official sentences him to one year of penal servitude,
the days of labor are also calculated in terms of the labor service exemption tax
and may cancel the full value of the copper to be paid for redemption.
Whether taxes are completely replaced or not
follows the explanation above.
COMMENTARY:
Each year of increase due to subversion of the law
cancels two years.
If not a full year,
but more than fifty days,
it replaces one year.
[16a]SUBCOMMENTARY:
One year of penal servitude due to subversion of the law
completely cancels two years of taxes and labor services.
Three years
cancels six years of taxes and labor services....
In accordance with the statute,
fifty days of an adult's labor
replaces one year and gets exemption from both taxes and labor services.83. 83Niida, Statutes, p. 668; Twitchett, Financial Administration, p. 141.
. . In all cases, a year means three hundred sixty days.
COMMENTARY:
If there are no taxes and labor services for the corresponding year,
then they are canceled for the following year.
Military service
is canceled by days.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
Where penal servitude is due to subversion of the law
(because of imperial grace)
and there are no taxes and labor services because of imperial grace or because of flood or drought,
they are canceled in the following year.
Military service
is canceled by the days of the next turn of duty.
Where one year of penal servitude is due to subversion of the law,
it replaces two years' service duties.
QUERY:
The article refers to the following year being canceled.
But suppose because of drought or flood or a grant of imperial grace once again there are no taxes or labor services.
Are these then canceled in a later year or not?
REPLY:
The article states that if there are no taxes and labor services for the corresponding year,
then they are canceled for the following year.
The article pities those whose increase of penal servitude and labor was due to subversion of the law
and allows them cancelation of taxes and labor services for the following year.
If in the next year there are no taxes and labor services,
this is put off until the following year
[32] when both are required.
The basic desire is that they be canceled.
Where there has been an imperial grace or frost or drought,

according to the statute, there is exemption from both taxes and labor services.84 84Niida, Statutes, p. 676; Twitchett, Financial Administration, p. 144. The extent of the remission depended upon what percentage of the crop was destroyed.
How can this be considered as the year [in which taxes and labor services are canceled because of increased sentence]?
[16b] If the people have already labored and paid taxes,
these are canceled for the following year.
If in such a later year there are no taxes and labor services,
these must be canceled for a year in which there are such taxes and labor services.
The principle is the same,
and no other opinions are possible.
ARTICLE: 44.4—In cases where penal servitude was originally required
and where beating with the heavy or light stick has already been carried out,
the value of the copper for redemption of beating with the heavy or light stick
decreases the years of penal servitude accordingly.
SUBCOMMENTARY:
If the original sentence was one year of penal servitude
and the officials have already had one hundred blows with the heavy stick
administered when the matter is discovered,
the criminal is returned and sentenced to penal servitude.
The one hundred blows with the heavy stick that have already been administered
cannot be withdrawn.
One year of penal servitude is redeemed by payment of twenty chin of copper,
which is eighteen days of penal servitude for each chin,
corresponding to ten blows with the light stick.
The previously administered one hundred blows with the heavy stick
altogether reduce the penal servitude to one hundred eighty days.
Thus the ten chin of copper
cancel one-half year of penal servitude.
If for a punishment of one year of penal servitude the criminal had already been beaten fifty blows with the light stick,
then the five chin of copper
would reduce the penal servitude labor by ninety days.
For the remaining penal servitude, aside from that which has been reduced,
each criminal is sent into labor in accordance with the ordinance.
CHAPTER VI
ARTICLE: 45.1a-i—In all cases where two or more offenses are discovered together,
the heavier punishment is sentenced.11Regarding multiple offenses, see also translation Chapter IV, note 1. The situation described here brings the lightest punishment to the criminal.

QUERY:
A person takes bribes of goods worth fifteen p'i of silk and subverts the law.

REPLY:
If the illicit goods taken as a bribe to subvert the law
come from a single person,
then even though what was discovered first has already been sentenced,
what was discovered later
must be combined with it
so that the whole crime is sentenced.
This is not the same as a repeated crime in which only the illicit goods present are combined.

the sentence is strangulation.
However, those officials who have no salary

are sentenced following the law on reduction of punishment. 2222That is, following Article 138, their punishment is reduced one degree. Persons working in government offices who had no official rank are not listed in the statute on salaries. See Niida, Statutes, p. 321.
FURTHER QUERY:
If ten persons in business together
have their capital goods in one place
and the thieves take them away at one time,
is this the same as a repeated [3b] crime or not?
[35] REPLY:
The commentary on this article states that
if a supervisory or custodial official takes bribes because of some matter, or is given goods in connection with the same matter,
or if the official repeatedly takes bribes because of one matter, or if he commits repeated robberies within his area of supervision,
the illicit goods are combined but not halved.
But aside from these three crimes,
all others are sentenced for one-half the value of the goods.
If the goods of ten persons
are taken together at one time,
although this seemingly is not a repeated crime
yet the owners of the goods are different persons.
The goods are not those of a single person
and in principle it is the same as robbery being committed ten times.
Thus it is sentenced the same as a repeated crime,
and the illicit goods are reduced by half.
But if the goods had been transferred to one person's sole charge
and lost, replacement would also be his sole charge.
In principle, they would then be the same as one man's goods,
and the crime would not be considered as repeated robbery.

Not equal

are punished less heavily.24 24The maximum punishment for robbery by stealth is life exile with added labor, and that for taking goods within the area under one's supervision is three years of penal servitude.
Therefore they are called not equal.

refers to a person repeating the crime of robbery by stealth at different places

Further, if the crime of robbery by force is repeated in different places

Now if the goods worth nine p'i of silk from the robberies by force

ARTICLE: 46.1a—All cases involving those who dwell together
or relatives of the third or closer degree of mourning, including maternal grandparents, grandsons in the female line,

allow mutual concealment should one of them commit a crime ,3838See the discussion on the family in the fifth part of introduction Chapter II. The basis of this article goes back to a supposed saying of Confucius. "Confucius said, 'Among us in our part of the country, those who are upright are different from this. The father conceals the misconduct of the son, and the son conceals the misconduct of the father. Uprightness is to be found in this.' " Lun-yü, xIII, 18.2; Legge, The Chinese Classics, I, 270.
SUBCOMMENTARY:

(maternal grandparents, grandsons in the female line, the wives of grandsons in the male line, and a husband's brothers and their wives)
But even though the mourning relationship with maternal grandparents, grandsons in the female line, the wives of grandsons in the male line, and a husband's brothers and their wives is slight,
the circumstances of their being relatives are important.
Therefore, should there be an offense, they conceal each other's crimes and make no accusations.
In this case, however, maternal grandparents do not include the maternal great- and great-great-grandparents,

and grandsons in the female line do not include the great- and great-great-grandsons.3939References in the Code to grandparents and grandchildren usually include the four ascending and decending generations. The reason for the limitation here is that the persons excluded do not come within the five degrees of mourning relationship.
